intro: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it, and owns the Galápagos Islands, where Charles Darwin found clues to evolution.

chapters.title: Early cultures
text: The Valdivia culture made some of the oldest pottery in the Americas, about 5,500 years ago. The Inca conquered the highlands in the late 1400s, and Quito became a northern Inca capital.

chapters.title: Spanish rule
text: Spain conquered the region in the 1530s. Quito's old town, full of baroque churches, is one of the best-preserved colonial centres in the Americas.

chapters.title: Independence and after
text: Ecuador won independence at the Battle of Pichincha in 1822, joined Gran Colombia and became a separate country in 1830. In 2000 it adopted the US dollar after an economic crisis. Since 2021 drug gangs have caused a surge in violence.

highlight.title: Darwin
highlight.text: Darwin's 1835 visit to the Galápagos helped inspire his theory of evolution.
